mainTopic: How high up the windpipe a שחיטה may be done: the rings of the קנה, the dispute about מוגרמת and רבי זירא's story, and the rulings about the tip of the cartilage and the חיטי.
overview: The גמרא finishes a ברייתא in which רבי יוסי בר יהודה permits slaughtering inside the smaller rings of the windpipe, and which also records a dispute about מוגרמת, a cut where the knife slid up out of the proper place. רב יוסף explains that רב ושמואל agree with רבי יוסי בר יהודה about the large ring but not about the smaller rings, meaning the הלכה follows him only on the large ring. רבי זירא then goes up to ארץ ישראל and eats a מוגרמת. He says the report that רב ושמואל forbade it came through רב יוסף, who learns from everyone. רב יוסף angrily answers that he learns from רב יהודה, who is so careful that he even reports his doubts about who said a ruling. The גמרא asks why רבי זירא did not keep the stringencies of בבל. אביי and רב אשי each give an answer, and רב יוסף explains a report from מחוזא allowing מוגרמת as a local custom. Finally, רבי יוחנן rejects ריש לקיש's very lenient ruling. Then there are two opposite traditions about whether a cut that meets the חיטי, or leaves part of them, is kosher.

steps.title: The ברייתא permits slaughter inside the other rings
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא of רבי יוסי בר יהודה continues: slaughtering inside the smaller rings is valid, because they go around most of the windpipe.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone slaughters inside the other rings, even though they don't go all the way around the windpipe, since they go around most of it, the שחיטה is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a ברייתא it began quoting just before this. Here רבי יוסי בר יהודה says you may also slaughter inside the smaller rings of the windpipe.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, רב ושמואל said that רבי יוסי בר יהודה permitted slaughter only inside the large top ring. This ברייתא shows him permitting the other rings as well, because each one goes around most of the קנה. That is a direct contradiction to how רב ושמואל described his view.

keyTerms.meaning: The rings of cartilage that make up the windpipe
The windpipe, one of the two organs cut in שחיטה
Most of something; going around most of the windpipe is enough
His slaughter is valid

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a new statement. It is the end of a ברייתא the גמרא already started quoting, and it is being used against what רב ושמואל said about רבי יוסי בר יהודה.

phrases.english: One who slaughters in the rest of the rings,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין מַקִּיפוֹת אֶת כׇּל הַקָּנֶה,
phrases.english: even though they do not encircle the entire windpipe,
since they encircle the majority of the windpipe,
his slaughter is valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא quoted before this section began.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ושמואל's claim that רבי יוסי בר יהודה permitted only the large ring.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא has רבי יוסי בר יהודה explicitly permitting the other rings too.

steps.title: The dispute about a diverted cut
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא adds that a מוגרמת is invalid, but רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס testified that it is valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: A diverted cut is invalid. רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס testified about a diverted cut that it is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The same ברייתא adds a second case: what happens if the knife slid up out of the proper area. One view says it is invalid, and רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס testified that it is valid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מוגרמת is a cut where the knife moved up past the place where שחיטה is allowed. The ברייתא records two opinions on it. This dispute comes back later, in the story of רבי זירא (step 6) and in אביי's report from מחוזא (step 14).

keyTerms.meaning: A cut where the knife slipped up out of the proper area for שחיטה
Invalid; the animal may not be eaten
He testified, meaning he reported a tradition he had received

phrases.english: And a diverted cut is invalid.
phrases.notes: This is when the knife slid up above the ring, out of the place where you are allowed to slaughter.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina ben Antigonus testified
about a diverted cut that it is valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The ברייתא continues with a related case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מוגרמת is invalid according to the ברייתא, but רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס testified that it is valid.

steps.title: רב יוסף: two separate rulings
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף explains that רבי יוסי בר יהודה made two rulings, and רב ושמואל agree with one of them and disagree with the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: רבי יוסי בר יהודה is saying two things. רב ושמואל agree with him on one and disagree with him on the other.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers the contradiction. רבי יוסי בר יהודה permitted both the large ring and the other rings, and רב ושמואל accept only the first of these.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא really does quote רבי יוסי בר יהודה permitting the other rings, so רב יוסף does not deny it. He says רב ושמואל knew this and chose to follow him only on the large ring. They disagree with him on the smaller rings.

keyTerms.meaning: Two things
They hold like him, meaning they agree with him
They disagree with him

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר יְהוּדָה תַּרְתֵּי קָאָמַר.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei bar Yehuda is saying two things.
phrases.notes: The two things are: the large ring is permitted, and the other rings are permitted.

phrases.english: Rav and Shmuel hold like him in one,
and disagree with him in one.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר יְהוּדָה תַּרְתֵּי קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised by the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the opinion into two parts
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב ושמואל misreported רבי יוסי בר יהודה as permitting only the large ring.
steps.terutzMaskana: He permitted both. רב ושמואל follow him only on the large ring.

steps.title: But they said 'he did not say'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that רב ושמואל's actual words were that רבי יוסי בר יהודה 'did not say' anything about the other rings.
steps.simpleTranslation: But they said 'he did not say'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב יוסף. רב ושמואל used the words 'he did not say', which sounds like a report of his view, not a disagreement with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רב ושמואל just disagreed, they would say 'we don't hold like him.' Saying 'he did not say' sounds like they are describing what רבי יוסי בר יהודה himself held. So רב יוסף's answer seems not to fit their wording.

keyTerms.meaning: But surely; opens a challenge
He did not say; the exact words of רב ושמואל

phrases.english: But surely they are saying "he did not say"?
phrases.notes: This refers back to רב ושמואל's earlier words: even רבי יוסי בר יהודה said this only about the large ring.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב יוסף's answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's claim that רב ושמואל knowingly disagreed with רבי יוסי בר יהודה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The words 'he did not say' describe רבי יוסי בר יהודה's own position, which does not match a disagreement.

steps.title: They meant the הלכה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that רב ושמואל meant the הלכה follows him on the large ring but not on the other rings.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what they meant: the הלכה is like him regarding the large ring, and the הלכה is not like him regarding the other rings.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reinterprets רב ושמואל's words. 'He did not say' really means 'for הלכה, we don't follow what he said about the other rings.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wording is read as a ruling about the final הלכה, not as a report of רבי יוסי בר יהודה's view. This keeps רב יוסף's answer in place and fits the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what he means; the גמרא is reinterpreting the words
The practical law follows his view
The large ring at the top of the windpipe

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב ושמואל, you may slaughter inside the large ring, but not inside the smaller rings, even though רבי יוסי בר יהודה permitted both.

phrases.english: This is what he is saying:
the halacha is like him regarding the large ring,
and the halacha is not like him regarding the other rings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge about the wording.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'He did not say' was a report of רבי יוסי בר יהודה's view.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is a ruling about the הלכה: follow him on the large ring only.

steps.title: רבי זירא eats a מוגרמת in ארץ ישראל
steps.stepSummary: When רבי זירא went up to ארץ ישראל, he ate meat from a מוגרמת, which רב ושמואל had forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבי זירא went up, he ate a diverted cut that רב ושמואל had forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story. רבי זירא moved from בבל to ארץ ישראל and ate a מוגרמת, which was the issue רב ושמואל had ruled on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This connects back to the מוגרמת dispute in the ברייתא. רב ושמואל held it is invalid, and in ארץ ישראל they held it is valid. The story sets up the question of why רבי זירא, who came from בבל, did not follow רב ושמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: Went up, meaning moved from בבל to ארץ ישראל
He ate

phrases.english: When Rabbi Zeira went up,
phrases.notes: He went up from בבל to ארץ ישראל.

phrases.english: he ate the diverted cut of Rav and Shmuel.
phrases.notes: The kind of מוגרמת that רב ושמואל had ruled invalid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns to the מוגרמת dispute through a story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In ארץ ישראל רבי זירא treated a מוגרמת as permitted.

steps.title: Aren't you from רב ושמואל's place?
steps.stepSummary: The scholars of ארץ ישראל challenge רבי זירא for not following the rulings of his home authorities.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: Aren't you from the place of רב ושמואל?
steps.whatsHappening: The people there question רבי זירא. Since he came from בבל, where רב ושמואל are the authorities, shouldn't he keep their ruling?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumes a person should follow the rulings of the authorities of the place he comes from. Since רב ושמואל forbade מוגרמת, רבי זירא should not have eaten it.

keyTerms.meaning: From the place of; from the region where these sages are the authorities
Isn't it so that, used to open a challenge

phrases.english: They said to him:
Aren't you from the place of Rav and Shmuel?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי זירא's action.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A person from רב ושמואל's region should follow their ruling, which forbids it.

steps.title: The report came from רב יוסף
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא answers that the report of רב ושמואל's ruling came from יוסף בר חייא, who learns from everyone and may have heard it from an unreliable source.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: Who said it? יוסף בר חייא! יוסף בר חייא learns from everyone.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא defends himself by doubting the report. He says the ruling in the name of רב ושמואל was passed on by רב יוסף, who learns from all kinds of people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי זירא does not argue with רב ושמואל. He questions whether they really said it. Since רב יוסף took teachings from everyone, the report may have come from someone who quoted them wrongly, so רבי זירא did not feel bound by it.

keyTerms.meaning: Who said it? Asking who passed on the teaching
He learns from everyone, so not every report of his is reliable

steps.whatToRemember: רבי זירא ate a מוגרמת because he doubted that רב ושמואל really forbade it. The report came through רב יוסף, who learned from everyone.
steps.confusionAlert: יוסף בר חייא is רב יוסף himself, the same sage who answered in step 3. רבי זירא is not saying רב יוסף is a weak scholar, only that he took traditions from many people, some of whom may have quoted wrongly.

phrases.english: He said to them: Who said it?
Yosef bar Chiyya!
phrases.notes: This is רב יוסף, who passed on the ruling in רב ושמואל's name.

phrases.aramaic: יוֹסֵף בַּר חִיָּיא מִכּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא גְּמִיר.
phrases.english: Yosef bar Chiyya learns from everyone.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge to רבי זירא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Questioning whether the teaching was passed on reliably
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב ושמואל definitely forbade מוגרמת, so רבי זירא should follow them.
steps.terutzMaskana: The report is uncertain because רב יוסף learned from everyone, so רבי זירא was not bound by it.

steps.title: רב יוסף is upset and defends his source
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף hears that רבי זירא doubted his report. He angrily says he does not learn from just anyone. He learns from רב יהודה, who is extremely careful.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף heard this and got angry. He said: Do I learn from just anybody? I learn from רב יהודה, who even reports his own doubts about which person said something.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף pushes back against רבי זירא's claim that his report might come from an unreliable source. He says his teacher is רב יהודה, who is very careful.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 8, רבי זירא said that יוסף בר חייא learns from everyone, so his report about רב ושמואל might be wrong. רב יוסף answers that his source is רב יהודה, who is so exact that he even tells you when he is unsure who said a ruling. So his report should be trusted.

keyTerms.meaning: He became angry or upset
I learn / I learned
Doubts about which men said something
He recites or reports, as part of his learning

steps.confusionAlert: רב יוסף here is the same person as יוסף בר חייא from step 8. He is answering רבי זירא's comment about him.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef heard, and became angry.
phrases.notes: רב יוסף is the יוסף בר חייא whom רבי זירא just called someone who learns from everyone.

phrases.english: He said: Do I learn from just everyone?
I learn from Rav Yehuda,
who even reports doubts about which men said things.
phrases.notes: He means that רב יהודה is so careful that when he isn't sure who said a ruling, he says so.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבי זירא's reason in step 8 for doubting the report.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רבי זירא's claim that the report of רב ושמואל's ruling may come from an unreliable source.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The report actually comes from רב יהודה, who is extremely careful about who said what.

steps.title: Proof that רב יהודה is careful about who said what
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף gives an example. רב יהודה reports a ruling from רבי ירמיה בר אבא and says openly that he is not sure if it came from רב or from שמואל. The ruling is that three people can permit a בכור where there is no expert.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said that רבי ירמיה בר אבא said, and he was not sure whether it was in the name of רב or of שמואל: Three people can permit a בכור in a place where there is no expert.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף shows an example of how careful רב יהודה is. רב יהודה even admits when he is unsure which sage said a ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling about the בכור matters here only as an example of carefulness. רב יהודה did not just pick one name. He told us honestly that it was either רב or שמואל. Someone this exact would not pass on a ruling from an unreliable source.

keyTerms.meaning: A firstborn male kosher animal, which may only be slaughtered and eaten if it has a blemish
An expert who is qualified to judge blemishes
Three ordinary people can permit, acting as a court
A doubt or uncertainty

steps.confusionAlert: Don't get distracted by the law of the בכור. It has nothing to do with מוגרמת. It is only quoted to show how carefully רב יהודה reports names.

phrases.english: As Rav Yehuda said:
Rabbi Yirmeya bar Abba said,
possibly in the name of Rav,
possibly in the name of Shmuel:
Three people may permit the firstborn animal
phrases.notes: This means they may declare that its blemish is a real one, so it can be slaughtered and eaten.

phrases.english: in a place where there is no expert.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה: אָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה בַּר אַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the evidence for רב יוסף's claim in step 9.
steps.raayaObject: רב יהודה is a careful and reliable reporter of what רב and שמואל said.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב יהודה's report from רבי ירמיה בר אבא, where he openly states his doubt about whether it was רב or שמואל.

steps.title: Shouldn't רבי זירא keep the stringencies of the place he left?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks a new question. A person who moves keeps the stringencies of the place he left and of the place he arrived at. So why did רבי זירא, who came from בבל, eat מוגרמת in ארץ ישראל?
steps.simpleTranslation: Doesn't רבי זירא hold the rule that a traveler must keep both the stringencies of the place he left and the stringencies of the place he went to?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי זירא's behavior in a new way. Even in ארץ ישראל, shouldn't he keep the strict rules of בבל, where he came from?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now the question was whether רב ושמואל really forbade מוגרמת. Now the גמרא says: even if ארץ ישראל allows it, there is a known rule that a traveler keeps the strict customs of his hometown. רב ושמואל's ban was a בבל stringency, so רבי זירא should have kept it.

keyTerms.meaning: He does not hold of / does not accept
We place upon him, meaning he is obligated
The stringencies of a place, meaning its strict customs

phrases.english: And does Rabbi Zeira not hold

phrases.aramaic: נוֹתְנִין עָלָיו חוּמְרֵי הַמָּקוֹם שֶׁיָּצָא מִשָּׁם
phrases.english: that we place upon him the stringencies of the place he left
and the stringencies of the place he went to?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets aside the question of whether the report is reliable and raises a separate problem with רבי זירא's behavior.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי זירא's eating of מוגרמת in ארץ ישראל.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A traveler keeps the stringencies of his original place. רבי זירא came from בבל, where רב ושמואל forbade מוגרמת, so he should have kept that ban.

steps.title: אביי: Babylonians follow ארץ ישראל
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the traveler's rule applies within בבל, within ארץ ישראל, or when going from ארץ ישראל to בבל. But someone going from בבל to ארץ ישראל simply follows ארץ ישראל, because בבל is subordinate to it.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: That rule applies when going from one place in בבל to another, from one place in ארץ ישראל to another, or from ארץ ישראל to בבל. But from בבל to ארץ ישראל, since we are subordinate to them, we act like them.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי limits the traveler's rule. It does not apply when a Babylonian moves to ארץ ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule of keeping your hometown's stringencies assumes the two places are equals. בבל, however, looks to ארץ ישראל as its higher authority. So a Babylonian who comes to ארץ ישראל drops his old customs and follows the local practice, which explains why רבי זירא ate the מוגרמת.

keyTerms.meaning: These words apply only to... (a limiting phrase)
We are subordinate to them, we bow to their authority
We act in accordance with them

phrases.english: Abaye said: These words apply
from Bavel to Bavel,
and from Eretz Yisrael to Eretz Yisrael,
or also from Eretz Yisrael to Bavel,
but from Bavel to Eretz Yisrael,
since we are subordinate to them,
phrases.notes: "We" means the people of בבל, who accept the authority of ארץ ישראל.

phrases.english: we act like them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 11 by limiting the traveler's rule.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of a rule (הני מילי)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The traveler's rule applies everywhere, so רבי זירא had to keep the stringencies of בבל.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule does not apply from בבל to ארץ ישראל, because בבל follows ארץ ישראל's authority.

steps.title: רב אשי: רבי זירא did not plan to go back
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי gives a different answer. Even when moving from בבל to ארץ ישראל, the traveler's rule applies only to someone who plans to return home. רבי זירא had no plan to return.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Even if you say the rule applies from בבל to ארץ ישראל, it only applies when the person plans to go back. רבי זירא was not planning to go back.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי offers a second way to answer the question. The rule only binds a visitor who intends to return, and רבי זירא had moved for good.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי does not need אביי's idea that בבל is subordinate. Instead he limits the rule to someone who is only visiting. A person who has truly moved becomes a local and follows the new place, so רבי זירא could follow ארץ ישראל's practice.

keyTerms.meaning: Even if you say, meaning even if we grant your assumption
His intention is to return home

steps.whatToRemember: There are two answers for why רבי זירא could eat מוגרמת in ארץ ישראל. According to אביי, people from בבל always follow ארץ ישראל. According to רב אשי, the traveler's rule only applies to someone who plans to return, and רבי זירא had moved there permanently.
steps.whyThisMatters: These two answers set up important limits on the general rule of keeping the customs of the place you left. One limit depends on which place has authority, and the other depends on whether the person intends to return.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
Even if you say the rule applies from Bavel to Eretz Yisrael,
that applies only where he intends to return,

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי זֵירָא אֵין דַּעְתּוֹ לַחֲזוֹר הֲוָה.
phrases.english: and Rabbi Zeira was someone who did not intend to return.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different answer than אביי to the question of step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the rule based on the traveler's intention
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Anyone moving from בבל to ארץ ישראל must keep the stringencies of בבל.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only someone who plans to return keeps his hometown's stringencies, and רבי זירא did not plan to return.

steps.title: אביי cites a report from מחוזא that מוגרמת is kosher
steps.stepSummary: אביי tells רב יוסף that the rabbis from מחוזא report, in the name of רבי זירא from רב נחמן, that מוגרמת is kosher.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to רב יוסף: But the Sages who came from מחוזא say that רבי זירא said in the name of רב נחמן that a diverted slaughter is kosher!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי brings a report that clashes with the strict ruling רב יוסף has been defending. He asks how that can be.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף reported that מוגרמת is not kosher. Now אביי says there is a tradition, coming through רבי זירא himself, that it is kosher. So either the report is wrong or the two rulings conflict.

keyTerms.meaning: מחוזא, a large Jewish town in בבל
Kosher, a valid slaughter

phrases.english: Abaye said to Rav Yosef:
But don't the Sages who came from Mechoza say,

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said in the name of Rav Nachman:
a diverted slaughter is kosher!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the question of מוגרמת after the side discussion about a traveler's stringencies
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's report that מוגרמת is not kosher
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another tradition, through רבי זירא from רב נחמן, says מוגרמת is kosher

steps.title: Each place follows its own custom
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers that every river has its own course: each place follows its own practice.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Each river has its own course.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers אביי with a short saying: different places have different customs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף does not reject the report from מחוזא. He says that in מחוזא they followed רב נחמן and allowed מוגרמת, while other places followed the stricter view. Both traditions can be true, each in its own place.

keyTerms.meaning: Each river and its own course, meaning each place keeps its own custom

steps.whyThisMatters: This saying shows how the גמרא can accept two opposite practices as local customs, without calling either one a mistake.

phrases.english: He said to him:
Each river has its own course.
phrases.notes: He means each town follows its own rabbi's ruling, and in מחוזא they ruled like רב נחמן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge
steps.terutzResolutionType: Local custom: both rulings are kept, each in a different place
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The report from מחוזא contradicts רב יוסף's tradition
steps.terutzMaskana: מחוזא had its own custom, and that does not cancel the ruling elsewhere

steps.title: ריש לקיש allows a cut at the tip of the top cartilage
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן לקיש ruled that a cut at the very tip of the thyroid cartilage, above the big ring, is kosher.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן לקיש ruled kosher a cut at the tip of the cap cartilage.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story about how high up a kosher cut may go. רבי שמעון בן לקיש allowed a cut even at the tip of the top cartilage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a very lenient position. It allows a cut even higher than the big ring, at the edge of the cartilage that sits on top of the windpipe.

keyTerms.meaning: The tip of the 'cap', the top cartilage of the windpipe (the thyroid cartilage)
He ruled it kosher

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish ruled kosher
a cut at the tip of the cap cartilage.
phrases.notes: The 'cap' is the large cartilage that sits on top of the windpipe, above the big ring.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ אַכְשַׁר בְּחוּדָּא דְּכוֹבָעָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new case about the upper limit of a kosher cut
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A cut at the tip of the top cartilage is kosher

steps.title: רבי יוחנן says ריש לקיש went too far
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן objects to ריש לקיש's ruling, saying he stretched the kosher area much too far.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן proclaimed about him: He went far, far beyond the limit!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן reacts to ריש לקיש's ruling and rejects it as far too lenient.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן does not give a detailed argument. He simply says the ruling went way past the border of where a kosher cut can be.

keyTerms.meaning: He went far beyond, he greatly overstepped the limit
He called out about him, he said a sharp remark about him

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan called out about him:
"He went far, far over the limit!"

steps.triggerLanguage: קָרֵי עֲלֵיהּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן גִּיסָא גִּיסָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the lenient ruling in step 16
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole ruling of ריש לקיש
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It allows a cut far above the proper area of שחיטה

steps.title: A cut that meets the חיטי is a טרפה
steps.stepSummary: רב פפי in the name of רבא rules that if the cut met the small cartilage pieces called חיטי, the animal is a טרפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפי said in the name of רבא: If he met the חיטי cartilage, it is a טרפה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא sets a limit at the top of the windpipe. If the cut reaches the חיטי, the שחיטה is not valid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חיטי are small pieces of cartilage near the top ring, just under the tip of the 'cap'. They are outside the kosher area, so a cut there fails. The ruling uses the word 'met', which the גמרא will now ask about.

keyTerms.meaning: Small cartilage pieces at the top of the windpipe, near the top ring (the arytenoid cartilage)
He met, he came to
Not kosher, forbidden to eat

phrases.english: Rav Pappi said in the name of Rava:
If he met the chitei cartilage, it is a tereifa.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a clear upper limit, continuing the topic of how high a cut may go
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A cut that meets the חיטי makes the animal a טרפה

steps.title: What does 'met' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether 'met' means actually touching the חיטי, or only coming near them, and brings a פסוק for each meaning.
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: Does 'met' mean met and touched them, as it is written, 'and he met him (that is, struck him) and he died'? Or perhaps it means met without touching, as it is written, 'and the angels of God met him'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what רבא meant by the word 'met'. It shows that the word is used both ways in the תנ"ך.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'met' means touched, then only a cut that actually goes into the חיטי is a טרפה. If it means only came near them, then even a cut close to the חיטי is a טרפה, which is stricter.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was raised before the Sages, an open question
Touched
Or perhaps

phrases.english: A question was asked:
does 'met' mean he met and touched them,
as it is written, "And he met him and he died,"
or perhaps met but did not touch,
as it is written, "And the angels of God met him"?
phrases.notes: בראשית 32:2. The angels just met יעקב, with no touching.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the meaning of the key word in רבא's ruling
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does 'met' (פגע) mean touching the חיטי or only reaching near them?

steps.title: Leaving part of the חיטי is kosher
steps.stepSummary: A teaching is brought: רב פפא in the name of רבא says that if the cut left part of the חיטי, the שחיטה is kosher.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: רב פפא said in the name of רבא: If he left some of the חיטי, it is kosher.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another teaching of רבא that helps answer the question. If the cut went through the middle of the חיטי and left some of them, it is kosher.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows that merely touching the חיטי does not by itself make the animal a טרפה. As long as part of the חיטי is left, the cut is still kosher.

keyTerms.meaning: He left over, part of it remained uncut

phrases.english: It was stated:
Rav Pappa said in the name of Rava:
If he left some of the chitei, it is kosher.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a related teaching of רבא that helps answer the question
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Cutting into the חיטי while leaving part of them is kosher, so touching alone does not make it a טרפה

steps.title: A second witness: רבי חייא בריה דרב אויא said the same
steps.stepSummary: רב אמימר בר מר ינוקא reports that רבי חייא son of רב אויא also told him that leaving part of the חיטי is kosher.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אמימר בר מר ינוקא said: I was standing before רבי חייא son of רב אויא, and he said to me: If he left some of the חיטי, it is kosher.
steps.whatsHappening: Another sage gives support to the same ruling. He heard it in person from his teacher.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing new is added to the law. The point is that a second, separate tradition confirms that leaving part of the חיטי is kosher.

keyTerms.meaning: I was standing before him, I was present with him

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אַמֵּימָר בַּר מָר יָנוֹקָא:
phrases.english: Rav Ameimar bar Mar Yenuka said:
I was standing before
Rabbi Chiya son of Rav Avya,
and he said to me:
If he left some of the chitei, it is kosher.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the ruling of step 20 with another tradition
steps.raayaObject: The ruling that leaving part of the חיטי is kosher
steps.raayaSupportSource: A personal report from רבי חייא son of רב אויא

steps.title: A third witness: מר זוטרא taught it publicly
steps.stepSummary: רבינא tells רב אשי that רב שמן of סוברא reported that מר זוטרא came to their town and taught publicly that leaving part of the חיטי is kosher.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to רב אשי: רב שמן of סוברא told me that מר זוטרא happened to come to our place and taught: If he left some of the חיטי, it is kosher.
steps.whatsHappening: A third tradition supports the same ruling. This time it was taught in a public lecture.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Again, no new law. Three separate traditions now agree that leaving part of the חיטי is kosher, which makes the ruling very strong before the next opinion disagrees.

keyTerms.meaning: He happened to come, he visited
He taught publicly, in a lecture

phrases.english: Ravina said to Rav Ashi:
Rav Shemen of Suvara told me,
Mar Zutra happened to come to our place
and taught publicly:
If he left some of the chitei, it is kosher.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third tradition supporting the same ruling
steps.raayaObject: The ruling that leaving part of the חיטי is kosher
steps.raayaSupportSource: מר זוטרא's public lecture, reported through רב שמן of סוברא

steps.title: מר בר רב אשי holds the exact opposite
steps.stepSummary: מר בר רב אשי rules that meeting the חיטי is kosher, and leaving part of the חיטי is a טרפה, the reverse of the earlier rulings.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר בר רב אשי said: If he met the חיטי, it is kosher. If he left some of the חיטי, it is a טרפה.
steps.whatsHappening: A different sage completely flips the earlier rulings. For him, meeting the חיטי is fine, but leaving part of them is a טרפה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before, the rule was: meeting the חיטי is a טרפה, but leaving part is kosher. מר בר רב אשי says the opposite on both points, so there are now two opposite traditions about the same cases.

keyTerms.meaning: He met the חיטי, the cut came to the cartilage pieces
He left part of the חיטי uncut

steps.whatToRemember: There are two opposite traditions about the חיטי. רבא (as reported by רב פפי and רב פפא) and others say: met is a טרפה, left part is kosher. מר בר רב אשי says: met is kosher, left part is a טרפה.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two sides. מר בר רב אשי reverses both rulings, so read each one carefully: 'met' and 'left' switch outcomes.

phrases.english: Mar bar Rav Ashi said:
If he met the chitei, it is kosher,
If he left some of the chitei, it is a tereifa.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite tradition to everything reported before
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Meeting the חיטי is kosher, and leaving part of the חיטי is a טרפה
